message.content: {"results":[{"n":"G1","evidence":"All five screenshots show the 3D bamboo scene rendering properly in Chrome without errors or a blank screen.","pass":true},{"n":"G2","evidence":"OrbitControls allows dragging, but there is no polar angle restriction in the code to keep the camera above ground, and screenshot 5 shows the camera zooming completely outside the grove into a white void (maxDistance = 45 exceeds the ~21m grove radius).","pass":false},{"n":"G3","evidence":"The scene uses only two main InstancedMeshes (340 stalks and 3400 leaf planes), one 2048x2048 shadow map, and a lightweight UnrealBloomPass, which will comfortably exceed 30 fps on a standard laptop.","pass":true},{"n":"1","evidence":"All five screenshots display a persistent UI bar in the bottom-left corner with instructional text and three interactive buttons ('Match Photo Angle', 'Ground Walk View', 'Wind: ON').","pass":false},{"n":"2","evidence":"In the animate() loop, windUniforms.uTime updates automatically on load with windOn = true, driving vertex shader sway on both the bamboo stalks and leaves.","pass":true},{"n":"3","evidence":"Screenshot 1 matches the steep upward worm's-eye camera angle and converging bamboo framing of the reference photo, including the overhanging dark branch at upper left.","pass":true},{"n":"4","evidence":"Screenshots 1–3 show dense foreground and background bamboo stalks with spacing and clustering comparable to the reference photo.","pass":true},{"n":"5","evidence":"While green hues are present, screenshots 1–3 are heavily washed out by white sky glare and intense white specular stripes, losing the rich deep greens and dusty teal tones of the reference photo.","pass":false},{"n":"6","evidence":"Neither the reference photo (which looks straight up into the canopy) nor the 3D scene contains a path or brushwood fence; the code only creates a plain green CircleGeometry ground.","pass":false},{"n":"7","evidence":"The scene reproduces the bright overhead overcast sky lighting filtering down from the zenith, matching the reference photo's upward-lit canopy.","pass":true},{"n":"8","evidence":"Screenshots 1–3 clearly show dark horizontal node rings with slight geometric bulges at regular intervals along every bamboo stalk.","pass":true},{"n":"9","evidence":"Screenshots 1–3 show noticeable variation in stalk diameter, and the instance placement code randomizes scaleR (0.68–1.23) and scaleY (0.82–1.14).","pass":true},{"n":"10","evidence":"Screenshots 1–3 show stalks leaning at varied angles and curving gently rather than standing on a rigid vertical grid.","pass":true},{"n":"11","evidence":"Screenshots 1–4 show the canopy composed of clusters of thin, narrow lanceolate bamboo leaves arranged in fan-like sprays.","pass":true},{"n":"12","evidence":"In section 9 of the code, the ground is just a flat CircleGeometry with a solid dark green MeshStandardMaterial (color: 0x1a2616) and no soil texture or fallen leaves.","pass":false},{"n":"13","evidence":"Screenshot 5 (zoomed out) clearly exposes the circular boundary of the finite bamboo cluster surrounded by empty white space.","pass":false},{"n":"14","evidence":"Screenshots 1–3 show uniform lighting and harsh vertical specular highlights along the stalks, with no dappled sunlight patches on the stalks or ground (leafInstanced does not cast shadows).","pass":false},{"n":"15","evidence":"Screenshots 1–3 show intense atmospheric bloom and bright haze bleeding between the upper stalks, creating depth separation.","pass":true},{"n":"16","evidence":"In screenshots 1–4, leaves against the bright sky appear brighter lime-green via emissive coloring and vertex color gradients, giving the impression of backlit foliage.","pass":true},{"n":"17","evidence":"In screenshots 1–4, shadowed areas on and between the stalks retain green-tinted dark tones from the hemisphere and bounce lights and never crush to pure black.","pass":true},{"n":"18","evidence":"Screenshots 1–3 show overly harsh, plastic-looking white specular streaks running down the stalks and uniform repeating bands without natural yellowing or convincing organic stains.","pass":false},{"n":"19","evidence":"In screenshot 4, close-up leaf clusters read as flat opaque cut-out planes with uniform painted gradients rather than genuinely translucent material.","pass":false},{"n":"20","evidence":"As defined in section 9 of the code and partially glimpsed between leaves in screenshot 4, the ground is an untextured solid-color flat disc and does not read as real soil, leaves, or stone.","pass":false},{"n":"21","evidence":"The camera intentionally pitches steeply upward (~78°) to match the worm's-eye reference photo with zero camera roll, keeping perspective convergence level and symmetrical in screenshot 1.","pass":true},{"n":"22","evidence":"The custom vertex shader on leafMat (section 7) displaces leaf clusters continuously using sine waves driven by uTime.","pass":true},{"n":"23","evidence":"In bambooMat.onBeforeCompile (section 5), horizontal wind displacement is multiplied by pow(hFactor, 2.1), keeping the base anchored at y=0 while bending increases exponentially toward the top.","pass":true},{"n":"24","evidence":"In sections 5 and 7, wind motion uses only fixed-amplitude periodic sine/cosine functions of uTime (e.g., sin(uTime * 0.85 + phase) * 0.32) with constant uWindStrength = 1.0, lacking varied gusts.","pass":false},{"n":"25","evidence":"There is no particle system, falling leaf geometry, or drifting dust implemented anywhere in the code or visible in the screenshots.","pass":false},{"n":"26","evidence":"Using continuous trigonometric functions of elapsed seconds (frequencies 0.72 to 2.4 rad/s and amplitudes 0.14–0.32m on 28m stalks) produces smooth, real-world sway speeds with no loop resets or jumps.","pass":true},{"n":"27","evidence":"All 340 stalks share one identical CylinderGeometry with a baked curveX = pow(vNorm, 1.85) * 0.65 and identical 26-repeat canvas texture, making repeating joint ring patterns visible on adjacent foreground stalks in screenshot 1.","pass":false},{"n":"28","evidence":"The scene uses static geometries with alphaTest = 0.32 on leaves (avoiding alpha-sorting flicker) and no LOD switching, preventing pop-in when orbiting.","pass":true},{"n":"29","evidence":"In screenshots 1–4, randomly rotated 2.7m leaf planes intersect and clip straight through nearby bamboo stalks (e.g., mid-ground stalks in screenshot 1 and right side of screenshot 4).","pass":false},{"n":"30","evidence":"Screenshot 1 immediately reads as stylized real-time CG due to the overlaid UI bar, blown-out white haze, harsh white specular stripes on uniform stalks, and untextured stick-like dark branch.","pass":false}]}
